books.section: Topic 4.10 The Second Great Awakening, Utopian Communities

stimulus.text: Two utopian communities tried to rebuild American life from scratch. Brook Farm, founded outside Boston in 1841 by the transcendentalist George Ripley, shared labor equally among its members and valued leisure as a way of becoming fuller human beings. New Harmony, founded in Indiana in 1825 by the Scottish industrialist Robert Owen, was built on principles of total equality. Both drew on European thinkers: Brook Farm on the French socialist Charles Fourier, New Harmony on Owen himself.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 6, Topic 4.10, Utopian Communities: Brook Farm established outside Boston in 1841 by George Ripley, equal sharing of labor and leisure; New Harmony founded by Robert Owen in 1825 around total equality; inspiration from Fourier and Owen. Original synthesis, not a quotation.

source: original; stimulus paraphrases Barron's on Brook Farm and New Harmony
stem: According to the passage, Brook Farm differed from most American workplaces of the 1840s in which way?

options.text: Brook Farm paid its workers the highest cash wages in New England
options.misconception: Wages were the era's measure of work, so a new community can look like a high-wage employer.

options.text: Brook Farm was owned by a single wealthy industrialist who set all the rules
options.misconception: Industrialists owned the mills, so a community can look like one man's factory.

options.text: Brook Farm forbade all leisure and required members to work every waking hour
options.misconception: Hard work was the era's virtue, so a serious community can look like all work and no rest.

options.text: Brook Farm shared labor equally and valued leisure as growth toward fuller humanity

rationales.A: Brook Farm shared labor, it did not pay top cash wages. Wages were the market's measure, and the community rejected that measure.
rationales.B: Brook Farm was a communal experiment, not one industrialist's property. Robert Owen founded New Harmony, but Brook Farm was Ripley's shared venture.
rationales.C: The passage says the opposite: Brook Farm valued leisure positively, as a means of becoming fuller human beings, against the era's worship of work.
rationales.D: Equal sharing of labor and a positive view of leisure are the passage's own words for Brook Farm, and both break with the market's workplace.
rationales.general:
1. Read the passage's own contrast: equal labor, and leisure valued as growth, not idleness.
2. Compare it with the mill or the farm: wages for work, and leisure treated as wasted time.
3. Name the difference: Brook Farm rebuilt work itself, sharing it and honoring rest.
Background: Brook Farm was started by the transcendentalist George Ripley outside Boston in 1841.
Remember: when a community praises leisure, it is arguing with a world that praises only work.
